title: Union forces under Halleck capture Corinth, Mississippi
description: The month-long siege of Corinth, Mississippi, ended when Union forces under Major General Henry W. Halleck took the town from retreating Confederate forces under General P. G. T. Beauregard. Corinth was a critical rail junction.

title: Emperor Petronius Maximus is killed by a mob while fleeing Rome
description: As a Vandal fleet under Geiseric sailed for Italy, the Western Roman emperor Petronius Maximus rode out of Rome alone and was stoned to death by an angry mob after 75 days on the throne. Three days later the Vandals took Rome and sacked it.

title: Johnston and Smith attack McClellan's army outside Richmond
description: Confederate forces under Joseph E. Johnston and G.W. Smith attacked George B. McClellan's Union army at Seven Pines, outside the Confederate capital of Richmond, Virginia. Johnston was wounded, and Robert E. Lee soon took command of the army.

title: Alfonso X is proclaimed king of Castile and León
description: Alfonso X became King of Castile, León and Galicia, reigning until his death in 1284; Castile and León had been permanently united since 1230. In 1257 a dissident faction chose him to be king of Germany, a claim he renounced in 1275.

title: Kentucky joins the Union as the fifteenth state
description: Kentucky, previously a part of Virginia, was admitted into the Union as the fifteenth state, after ten constitutional conventions in Danville and the consent of Virginia and Congress. Isaac Shelby, a military veteran from Virginia, was its first governor.

title: Benedict I is consecrated pope with imperial approval
description: Benedict I became bishop of Rome once imperial approval had come from Constantinople, as popes of the Byzantine Papacy needed for their consecration. His pontificate, to 579, fell during the Lombard expansion in Italy and a famine in Rome.

title: Bridget Bishop's trial opens the Salem witch trials
description: Bridget Bishop, accused of bewitching five young women, was the first case before the new Court of Oyer and Terminer at Salem, Massachusetts. She was hanged on 10 June, the first person executed for witchcraft in the Salem witch trials.

title: Norway and Novgorod make peace in the Treaty of Novgorod
description: The Treaty of Novgorod, a 10-year peace signed in Novgorod, ended decades of border skirmishes between Norway and Novgorod in Finnmark, in the far north. Novgorod had settled its conflict with Sweden in 1323 in the Treaty of Nöteborg.

title: Union troops rout Confederate forces at Philippi in Virginia
description: Union forces routed Confederate troops in and around Philippi, Virginia, in the clash also called the Philippi Races. It was the first organized land action of the American Civil War, though it is generally viewed as a skirmish rather than a battle.

title: Charles Emmanuel IV of Sardinia abdicates for his brother
description: Moved by the death of his wife, Clotilde of France, in March, Charles Emmanuel IV abdicated as King of Sardinia in favour of his brother Victor Emmanuel I. He kept the personal title of king and lived in Rome and Frascati.

title: The Louisiana Territory is renamed the Missouri Territory
description: After Louisiana entered the Union as a state, the Territory of Louisiana, formed in 1805 from the part of the Louisiana Purchase north of the 33rd parallel, was renamed the Missouri Territory. Part of it became the State of Missouri in 1821.

title: Theodora is crowned empress and marries Emperor Theophilos
description: Theodora was crowned empress in the Church of St Stephen in Daphne and then married the iconoclast emperor Theophilos in the Hagia Sophia. An iconophile, she later ruled as regent and restored the veneration of icons in 843.

title: Roger of Lauria defeats the Angevin fleet in the Gulf of Naples
description: In the War of the Sicilian Vespers, an Aragonese–Sicilian fleet under Roger of Lauria defeated an Angevin fleet in the Gulf of Naples and captured its commander, Prince Charles of Salerno. The victory helped secure Aragonese control of the sea around Sicily.
source: Battle of the Gulf of Naples

title: The Lo Mustang earthquake devastates Nepal
description: An earthquake of an estimated magnitude between 8.2 and 8.8 struck northern Nepal, also affecting southern China and northern India and causing severe damage in Kathmandu. It killed an approximate 30 percent of the Nepalese population of the time.

title: Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad fort
description: In a lavish ceremony at Raigad fort, before nearly fifty thousand people, Shivaji was crowned king as Gaga Bhatt poured over him the waters of seven sacred rivers. He took the titles Chhatrapati ("Lord of the Umbrella") and Shakakarta ("founder of an era").

title: The Gazeta de Buenos-Ayres publishes its first issue
description: The weekly Gazeta first served to publicise the acts of the Primera Junta, the first post-colonial Argentine government; Mariano Moreno wrote it at first, and it was read aloud in chapels. Argentina has honoured the day as Journalist's Day since 1938.
profile: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

title: Chilean troops storm the Morro de Arica in the War of the Pacific
description: Chilean forces assaulted and captured the Morro de Arica, a headland 139 metres high, from Peru, ending the Desert Campaign of the War of the Pacific. Chile went on to win the war, gaining resource-rich territory from Peru and Bolivia.

title: Silverius becomes bishop of Rome after the death of Agapetus I
description: The deacon Silverius rose to the papacy as the Ostrogothic king Theodahad sought to install a pro-Gothic candidate just before the Gothic War. The Byzantine general Belisarius later deposed him, and he starved to death in exile on Palmarola in 537.

title: British troops defeat the Continental Army at Trois-Rivières
description: A British army under Quebec Governor Sir Guy Carleton defeated Continental Army units under Brigadier General William Thompson trying to stop its advance up the Saint Lawrence River valley. This second defeat ended American operations in Quebec.

title: Duke Odo of Aquitaine defeats the Umayyads at Toulouse
description: Odo the Great, Duke of Aquitaine, defeated an Umayyad army under al-Samh ibn Malik al-Khawlani besieging Toulouse, the first major battle lost by the Umayyad forces in their campaign northwards. Pope Gregory II sent gifts to celebrate the victory.

title: Stonewall Jackson ends his Valley campaign with a win at Port Republic
description: Jackson's Army of the Valley won its most costly battle of the Shenandoah Valley campaign at Port Republic, in Rockingham County, Virginia. With Cross Keys it forced the Union armies to retreat, leaving Jackson free to reinforce Robert E. Lee near Richmond.

title: A landslide dam on the Dadu River bursts, flooding Sichuan
description: After an earthquake near Kangding on 1 June and an aftershock nine days later, a landslide dam across the Dadu River collapsed, causing a flood that extended 1,400 km downstream. About 100,000 people were killed.

title: Grant withdraws from Cold Harbor and moves his army south
description: Ulysses S. Grant pulled his Union troops from their position at Cold Harbor, Virginia, and moved south, leaving the battle to the Confederate army of Robert E. Lee. Thousands of Union soldiers had been killed or wounded in the frontal assault of 3 June.

title: Frederick Douglass helps found the American League of Colored Laborers
description: The first union created for African Americans in the United States held its first meeting at the Mother African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church in New York City. It faltered soon after; the Colored National Labor Union followed in 1869.

title: The Continental Congress founds the Continental Army
description: The Second Continental Congress took control of the Patriot forces outside Boston, forming the Continental Army, and John Adams nominated George Washington as its commander-in-chief. The army marks the birth of the United States Armed Forces.

title: Settlers in Sonoma rise against Mexico and proclaim a republic
description: In the Bear Flag Revolt, Anglo settlers in Sonoma rebelled against Mexico and proclaimed the California Republic, an unrecognized breakaway state. It controlled an area north of San Francisco and lasted until 9 July 1846.

title: The Yongle Emperor's army routs Bunyashiri's Mongols at the Onon
description: On the first of the Yongle Emperor's campaigns into Mongolia, the Ming army annihilated the forces of the Northern Yuan khagan Bunyashiri at the Onon River, though he escaped. The Ming then defeated Arughtai, who became a tributary of the Ming.
source: Yongle Emperor's campaigns against the Mongols

title: Pope Sergius II crowns Louis II king at Rome
description: Louis, eldest son of Emperor Lothair I, was crowned king and co-emperor at Rome by Pope Sergius II, a ceremony mirroring Lothair's own crowning. From 855 Louis ruled alone as king of Italy and emperor of the Carolingian Empire.

title: Napoleon defeats Blücher's Prussians at Ligny
description: Napoleon's Armée du Nord defeated part of a Prussian army under Blücher at Ligny, while Ney held Wellington at Quatre Bras. The bulk of the Prussian army survived and fought at Waterloo two days later; Ligny was Napoleon's last victory.

title: An earthquake in Kutch raises the Allah Bund in western India
description: An earthquake of estimated magnitude 7.7 to 8.2 struck the Rann of Kutch, triggering a tsunami and causing at least 1,543 deaths. It formed Sindri Lake and raised a ridge about 80 km long and 6 m high, the natural dam known as the Allah Bund.

title: Mumtaz Mahal dies in childbirth at Burhanpur
description: Mumtaz Mahal, chief consort of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, died in Burhanpur giving birth to her 14th child while accompanying him on a campaign in the Deccan. Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in Agra to house her tomb.

title: Empress Matilda marries Geoffrey of Anjou at Le Mans
description: Matilda, widow of Emperor Henry V and the nominated heir of Henry I of England, married Geoffrey, the son of Fulk of Anjou, at Le Mans; she was 25 and he was 13. The marriage proved difficult, and she soon left him for Normandy.

title: Normans rout the army of Pope Leo IX at Civitate
description: Normans under Humphrey of Hauteville, Count of Apulia, defeated a Swabian-Italian-Lombard army organised by Pope Leo IX in southern Italy. By 1059 the Normans had allied with the papacy, and Pope Nicholas II recognised their conquest in south Italy.

title: Pope Adrian IV crowns Frederick Barbarossa emperor
description: For fear of Roman hostility, Pope Adrian IV crowned Frederick Barbarossa emperor secretly on a Saturday instead of the usual Sunday, after a contest over ceremony at their meeting at Sutri. Two years later the word "holy" first appeared with his empire.

title: Bishops at the First Council of Nicaea adopt the Nicene Creed
description: The First Council of Nicaea, convened by the emperor Constantine I, adopted the original Nicene Creed, whose text ends with anathemas against Arian propositions. According to the traditional view, the creed was amended in 381 at Constantinople.

title: Hudson's Bay and North West Company men clash at Seven Oaks
description: In the Pemmican War, men of the Hudson's Bay Company and the North West Company fought a violent confrontation near modern-day Winnipeg, also called the Seven Oaks Massacre. The British government later forced the companies to merge.

title: Tarhoncu Ahmed Pasha becomes Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire
description: Tarhoncu Ahmed Pasha, an Ottoman Albanian statesman, was appointed grand vizier, the effective head of government, who held the imperial seal. He held office until March 1653, when he was executed because of the economic reforms he had begun.

title: The Treaty of Anagni seeks peace in the War of the Sicilian Vespers
description: Pope Boniface VIII, James II of Aragon, Philip IV of France, Charles II of Naples and James II of Majorca made an accord at Anagni confirming the Treaty of Tarascon of 1291. It also sought a diplomatic solution to the conquest of Sicily by Peter III of Aragon.

title: Abbasid caliph al-Muhtadi is murdered after his troops are beaten
description: After Musa ibn Bugha marched on the capital and defeated the troops loyal to him, the Abbasid caliph al-Muhtadi refused to abdicate and was murdered. His cousin al-Mu'tamid succeeded him, and his reign marks the end of the "Anarchy at Samarra".

title: The Battle of Jerusalem Plank Road begins near Petersburg
description: Two Union infantry corps tried to sever the Weldon Railroad near Petersburg, Virginia, but were attacked and driven off by the Confederate Third Corps, chiefly the division of William Mahone. The Union then began extending its siege lines west.

title: The Council of Ephesus opens to rule on Nestorius
description: Convened by the Roman emperor Theodosius II, the third ecumenical council met at the Church of Mary in Ephesus until 31 July. It confirmed the original Nicene Creed and condemned Nestorius, who preferred to call the Virgin Mary Christotokos over Theotokos.

title: Humayun defeats Sikandar Shah Suri at Sirhind and regains Delhi
description: A Mughal army under Humayun and Bairam Khan defeated the Afghan forces of Sikandar Shah Suri, the last ruling Sur sultan of Hindustan, at Sirhind. The loss of Delhi ended the Sur Empire's 15-year rule, and Humayun reigned again until his death in 1556.

title: Dragut dies of his wounds during the Great Siege of Malta
description: The Ottoman corsair and naval commander Dragut died five days after a piece of rock, thrown up by a cannonball striking near him, hit his head at the siege of Fort St. Elmo. His death set the senior Ottoman officers squabbling, which helped save the Knights.

title: Continental forces turn back the British at Springfield
description: A British force under Knyphausen and Sir Henry Clinton trying again to attack George Washington's army at Morristown, withdrew from Springfield as rebel forces arrived. The Continental victory effectively ended British ambitions in New Jersey.

title: A solar eclipse marks Mursili II's campaign against Hayasa-Azzi
description: In the tenth year of the Hittite king Mursili II, as he was about to launch a campaign against the Kingdom of Hayasa-Azzi, "the Sun gave a sign": an eclipse that most scholars date to this day. It is of great importance for dating the Hittite Empire.

title: Mieszko I of Poland defeats Margrave Hodo near the Oder
description: An army led by Mieszko I of Poland defeated the forces of the Saxon margrave Hodo near the Oder river, the first documented victory of Polish forces. Whether the battle took place near the modern town of Cedynia is disputed.

title: Lutheran princes present the Augsburg Confession to Charles V
description: At the Diet of Augsburg, German rulers and free cities presented Emperor Charles V with the Augsburg Confession, prepared by Philipp Melanchthon at the behest of John, Elector of Saxony. It became the primary confession of faith of the Lutheran Church.

title: The ascetic En no Ozunu is banished to Izu Ōshima
description: According to the chronicle Shoku Nihongi, the Imperial Court banished En no Ozunu, of Mount Katsuragi and acclaimed for his sorcery, to Izu Ōshima after he was accused of trickery with his magic. Folk religion holds him to be the founder of Shugendō.

title: Sher Shah Suri defeats the Mughal emperor Humayun at Chausa
description: Afghan forces under Sher Shah Suri, aided by the Ujjainiya Rajputs of Bhojpur, defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun at Chausa, southwest of Buxar in modern-day Bihar. Sher Shah went on to found the Sur Empire, with Delhi as his seat of power.

title: Johnston's Confederates repulse Sherman at Kennesaw Mountain
description: Union Major General William T. Sherman launched his most significant frontal assault of the Atlanta campaign against Joseph E. Johnston's Army of Tennessee in Georgia. It failed, but the Confederate win did not halt Sherman's advance on Atlanta.

title: Cherokee warriors defeat a British force at Echoee
description: In the Anglo-Cherokee War, fought during the French and Indian War, Cherokee warriors under Seroweh defeated a British and colonial force under Archibald Montgomerie at Etchoe Pass, near present-day Otto in Macon County, North Carolina.

skip: Trivial for a history site: the founding of a college fraternity (Sigma Chi).

title: A major earthquake strikes Syria, damaging Hama and Shaizar
description: One of the largest earthquakes to hit Syria, of estimated magnitude 7.7, struck early in the morning, badly damaging Hama, Shaizar, the Krak des Chevaliers and the cathedral of St. Peter in Antioch. It was part of a sequence along the Dead Sea Transform.

skip: The material is one sentence (bishop of Rome from 30 June 296 to his death in 304): too thin for an event.

title: Gustavus Adolphus founds the University of Tartu in Dorpat
description: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden, then campaigning in Germany, signed the foundation act of a university in Dorpat (Tartu), months before his death at Lützen. Now Estonia's national university, it was then the third oldest in the Kingdom of Sweden.

title: Lexell's Comet passes closer to Earth than any comet on record
description: The comet Charles Messier had discovered in June passed 0.015 astronomical units from Earth, about six times the distance to the Moon, the closest approach of any comet in recorded history. It has not been seen since 1770 and is lost.

title: The Quinault and Quileute sign a treaty ceding land to the US
description: At the Quinault River in the recently formed Washington Territory, the Quinault and Quileute peoples of the western Olympic Peninsula signed a treaty ceding their land to the United States. Congress ratified it on 8 March 1859.

title: Miltiades is elected pope, ending a vacancy in Rome
description: According to the Liberian Catalogue, Miltiades was elected bishop of Rome, ending the vacancy after the death of Pope Eusebius. During his pontificate Emperor Constantine issued the Edict of Milan in 313, giving Christianity legal status in the Roman Empire.

title: Albert of Habsburg defeats and kills King Adolf at Göllheim
description: After the prince-electors deposed Adolf of Nassau without any formal election and proclaimed Duke Albert I of Habsburg king, their forces met at Göllheim, where Adolf died. Albert ruled as King of Germany until his assassination.

title: Jack Cade's rebels cross London Bridge into the city
description: Rebels from South East England led by Jack Cade, protesting the corruption of the king's advisers and losses in France, entered London, where Cade struck the London Stone and declared himself Lord Mayor. Sham trials of accused officials followed.

title: Pope John XV canonises Ulrich of Augsburg
description: Only 20 years after his death, Ulrich, a former prince-bishop of Augsburg, was canonised by Pope John XV, after many miracles were said to have been wrought at his grave. He was the first saint to be canonised by a pope rather than by a local authority.

title: Epaminondas leads Thebes to victory over Sparta at Mantinea
description: Thebans under Epaminondas, with their allies, defeated the Spartans, Eleans, Athenians and Mantineans in a battle to decide which alliance would dominate Greece. Epaminondas died, and both sides were weakened, paving the way for Philip II of Macedon.

title: Mehmed Çelebi defeats his brother Musa at Çamurlu
description: The last battle of the Ottoman Interregnum pitted two sons of Bayezid I, Mehmed Çelebi and Musa Çelebi; Musa was captured and executed. Mehmed reunited the Ottoman Empire and ruled it as Mehmed I until his death in 1421.

title: The hermit Pietro da Morrone is elected pope as Celestine V
description: After more than two years of deadlock following the death of Nicholas IV, the cardinals elected the hermit Pietro da Morrone, in the last papal election that was not a conclave. As Celestine V he reigned five months before abdicating.

title: Ottoman raiders sack Żejtun in their last major attack on Malta
description: A Turkish force of sixty ships under Damat Halil Pasha landed 5,000 to 6,000 men in south-eastern Malta and sacked Żejtun and nearby villages. The Order's cavalry and the local inhabitants drove the raiders back to their ships.

title: Tyre surrenders to the Venetian Crusade
description: After a 19-week siege, Tyre surrendered on terms letting its citizens leave with their families and goods or stay with their homes guaranteed. It was the last Muslim seaport on the Levant but Ascalon to fall to the Crusaders.

title: US ships capture Monterey, the capital of Alta California
description: During the Mexican–American War, Commodore John Drake Sloat's ships captured Monterey, the Alta Californian capital, without firing a shot. Yerba Buena (present-day San Francisco) fell two days later, as the US conquest of California began.

title: An earthquake and tsunami strike Valparaíso and the coast of Chile
description: An earthquake of an estimated magnitude of 9.1–9.3 caused severe damage from La Serena to Chillán. The tsunami inundated the lower parts of Valparaíso and affected more than 1,000 km of Chile's coastline.

title: The Shinsengumi attack shishi plotters at the Ikedaya Inn
description: In Kyoto, the Shinsengumi, the Bakufu's special police force, fought an armed encounter with shishi, among them masterless samurai of the Chōshū, Tosa and Higo domains, at the Ikedaya Inn. The incident brought the Shinsengumi considerable fame.

title: The Jōgan earthquake and tsunami strike the Sendai plain
description: An earthquake of an estimated magnitude of at least 8.6, possibly 9.0, struck around Sendai in northern Honshu, and its tsunami caused widespread flooding of the Sendai plain. In 2001 its sand deposits were found more than 4.5 kilometres from the coast.

title: An earthquake and tsunami devastate Byzantine Phoenicia
description: An earthquake of estimated magnitude 7.5 struck Byzantine Phoenicia, and the tsunami it triggered brought great destruction to the province's coastal towns and sank many ships. The pilgrim of Piacenza put the dead at 30,000 for Berytus alone.

title: Liu Yu takes the throne and founds the Liu Song dynasty
description: Days after Emperor Gong, the last ruler of the Eastern Jin, yielded the throne to him under pressure, the regent Liu Yu became the first emperor of the Liu Song dynasty, first of the Southern dynasties. He ruled for only two years.

title: Emperor Hadrian dies at his villa at Baiae
description: Hadrian, Roman emperor since 117, died in his villa at Baiae aged 62 after a long illness. Buried first at Puteoli, his remains were later moved to Rome, and his ashes were placed with those of his wife Vibia Sabina in the Mausoleum of Hadrian.

title: Süleyman Çelebi defeats his brother Musa outside Edirne
description: In the Ottoman Interregnum, the war among the sons of Bayezid I, Süleyman Çelebi defeated his brother Musa Çelebi outside the Ottoman capital, Edirne. In 1411 Süleyman's army defected to Musa, and Süleyman was captured and strangled.

title: Ottobuono Fieschi is elected pope as Adrian V
description: A nine-day conclave chose Ottobuono Fieschi, a former papal envoy to England, to succeed Innocent V. As Adrian V he died on 18 August 1276, before he had been ordained to the priesthood.

title: Felix IV becomes pope, chosen by Theodoric the Great
description: Felix IV became bishop of Rome as the chosen candidate of the Ostrogoth king Theodoric the Great, who had imprisoned his predecessor, John I, for allegedly conspiring with Constantinople. The frail John had died of neglect and ill-treatment.

title: Zhu Di captures Nanjing, ending the Jingnan campaign
description: Aided by the betrayal of his brother Zhu Hui and cousin Li Jinglong, Zhu Di took the Ming capital Nanjing with little resistance; the imperial palace burned down, and three bodies found there were announced as the Jianwen Emperor, his wife and son.

title: Nicholas Kelly leads a revolt at the Charleston workhouse
description: An enslaved man named Nicholas Kelly led an insurrection in Charleston, South Carolina, wounding several guards with improvised weapons and freeing 37 enslaved people. Most were quickly captured, and Kelly and two others were tried and hanged.

title: A fire burns 47 acres just south of Chicago's Loop
description: The Chicago Fire of 1874 burned 47 acres south of the Loop, destroying 812 structures and killing 20 people. The neighbourhood's Jewish immigrants from Russia and Poland and its middle-class African-American families were displaced to other parts of the city.

title: Rome dedicates the Temple of Castor and Pollux in the Forum
description: A son of the dictator Aulus Postumius dedicated the temple his father had vowed before the victory at Lake Regillus, on the spot where, by legend, the Dioscuri had appeared in the Forum. It later served as a meeting place for the Senate.

title: The Residence Act creates a capital district on the Potomac
description: The Residence Act approved the creation of the capital district of the United States along the Potomac River, considered the founding date of Washington, D.C. Congress moved there from Philadelphia in 1800, and John Adams moved into the new White House.

title: Damasus II becomes pope and dies 23 days later
description: A native of Bavaria, Damasus II became bishop of Rome as the second of the German pontiffs nominated by Emperor Henry III. He died on 9 August, after one of the shortest papal reigns.

title: The Scillitan Martyrs are executed at Carthage for their faith
description: Twelve early Christians from the town of Scillium in North Africa were executed by the Roman Empire in Carthage, at the end of a wave of persecution under Marcus Aurelius. This is the earliest record of Christianity in that part of the world.

title: The Great Fire of Rome breaks out near the Circus Maximus
description: The fire started in the merchant shops around Rome's chariot stadium, the Circus Maximus, and burned for six days before it was brought under control, then reignited for three more. By the end, nearly three quarters of Rome had been destroyed.

title: Ramiro II of León defeats Abd al-Rahman III at Simancas
description: The troops of King Ramiro II of León met those of the Cordovan caliph Abd al-Rahman III near the walls of Simancas, and Ramiro defeated the caliph's army. Abd al-Rahman had raised the Emirate of Córdoba to a caliphate in 929.
